title: The White House — Public Tours
description: The White House at 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue NW, Washington, D.C., is the president's residence and office, built 1792-1800 to James Hoban's design and burned by the British in 1814. Public tours of the East Wing and state rooms are free but must be requested in advance through a Member of Congress, with security screening for all visitors. PUBLIC-RECORDS ONLY: this record uses officially published visitor information; no non-public layouts or security details are included.

title: U.S. Capitol Visitor Center
description: The U.S. Capitol Visitor Center is the public entrance to the Capitol building, offering free guided tours of the Rotunda, National Statuary Hall, and the crypt, booked through visitthecapitol.gov. The Capitol has housed Congress since 1800 and its dome, completed during the Civil War, is a national symbol. Gallery passes for House and Senate sessions are available through congressional offices. PUBLIC-RECORDS ONLY: published visitor information.
